title: Spike: does WebRTC work phone-to-phone on the Orbic AP?
description: Gate for everything else. Tiny page (/room-test) that opens two data channels and reports ICE candidate types, connect time and round-trip ms. Check: AP client isolation, mDNS host candidates (Android Chrome hides LAN IPs behind .local names), whether any STUN is needed (none: LAN only, no internet), HTTPS cert trusted on both devices. Result decides WebRTC-direct vs box relay as the default transport.
notes:
Built (uncommitted): room.go (/api/room signaling+relay, tests in room_test.go), roomtest.html served at /room-test, scripts/dev/room-test.mjs (passes on loopback: direct 2 ms, via box 1 ms). Route wired in ui.go, /room-test in uiserver.go, /api/room excluded from the onion door. STILL TO DO: build+deploy, then open /room-test on two real phones on the Orbic AP and copy the report here.
RESULT 2026-10-10 (Pixel 6a <-> moto g 2025, both on the Orbic AP, no STUN): WebRTC works. Path host/host udp, 1 host candidate each, none hidden as .local. Connect 109 ms and 342 ms. Direct RTT median 42 ms (min 33-35, p95 50), 0 of 20 lost, both directions. Via-box measure is a self-echo (phone->box->phone) median 30-36 ms, NOT a true A->box->B relay, so it understates the relay: a real relay path is roughly two such round trips. Observation: ~40 ms is Wi-Fi hop latency (phones in power-save), fine for party games/remote input, marginal for twitch. FINDING: the Pixel's room WebSocket was found CLOSED (readyState 3) after sitting idle in a tab, so its room (CDWF) was gone and the Moto got 'no such room'. room.js (pf-ajt.3) must reconnect and re-join, and rooms should survive a short drop.
close_reason: WebRTC direct works between two phones on the Orbic AP; direct is the default transport, relay is fallback. See notes.

title: Room channel: survive dropped WebSocket (grace period, reconnect, resume id)
description: Spike found a phone's /api/room socket closed while its tab sat idle (Android Chrome freezes background tabs). Box should keep a room and peer slot for ~60 s after a socket drops; page should reconnect with the same peer id and re-negotiate only if the data channel died. Also measure a true A->box->B relay RTT, not a self-echo.
notes:
Built: 60 s grace, id+token resume, away/back/leave events, pong, 90 s idle, client auto-reconnect with backoff and wake triggers, same-place on reload. Pending: real-phone check with the screen off for 1-2 minutes.
Phone test 2026-10-10 (Pixel screen off, Moto awake): phase A (~45 s): socket dropped, came back resumed=true same id, direct link stayed up, Moto saw nothing. Phase B (~2 min): Pixel socket dropped ~3 s after screen off and its next attempt hung in CONNECTING (Wi-Fi asleep), never recovered; Moto saw left:p1 at 61.7 s (grace expired, as designed). BUG in room.js: no connect timeout and no recovery for a hung attempt. FIXED in working tree (connectTimeout 8 s, _abandon, wake abandons a stale attempt), regression test added to scripts/dev/room-test.mjs; not yet committed/deployed/retested on the phones. Pixel has a lock screen (keyguard showing after wake): needs the user to unlock.
close_reason: Verified on phones: short outage resumes the same place (phase A); 2 min screen-off: Pixel re-joined afresh as p3 within 0.1 s of waking and the direct link was back 1.5 s later (grace expired as designed); hung-connect bug found and fixed (73eb172). A reload resumes the same place (seen by accident on the Moto).

title: Page: room.js client library (join, peers, data channels, relay fallback)
description: Served like /bt/btclient.js. API: room.create(), room.join(code), onPeer, send(to|all, msg), on('msg'). Tries WebRTC data channel per peer, falls back to box relay when ICE fails in 4 s, reconnects on screen sleep. Unordered/unreliable channel option for game input, reliable for files. Heartbeat and presence.
notes: Built: roomclient/room.js (served /room/room.js), /room-test rebuilt on it. Headless test scripts/dev/room-test.mjs passes (27 checks) and fails when resume is broken on purpose. NOT yet run on the phones; close after that.
close_reason: room.js built, tested headless (28 checks) and on a Pixel 6a + moto g 2025 (direct links, rejoin after screen-off). Deployed 73eb172.

title: Box: room signaling and relay endpoint (/api/room WebSocket)
description: room.go, reusing wsAccept/wsRead/wsOriginOK from btbridge.go and the login gate in ui.go. JSON text frames: join{room,name,role}, peers, offer/answer/ice (addressed by peer id), relay{to,data} fallback, leave. In-memory only, nothing stored or logged. Limits: rooms, peers per room (8), message size (16 KB), rate per peer, idle timeout, shed on btLoadNow() like the bridge. Room codes 4 letters from an unambiguous alphabet, expire when empty. LAN-only path (add to onionPathOK exclusions). Tests like btmux_test.go.
close_reason: room.go: signaling, relay, grace period, resume tokens, limits; Go tests + Chromium test pass. Deploy and phone run still to do.

title: Sign-in should return to the page that was asked for (keep #CODE after login)
description: A phone that scans a room QR while signed out lands on /login and, after signing in, on /ui: the room code in the link is lost and it must scan again. Login always redirects to /ui (uiserver.go). Add a safe return path: same-origin relative paths only (reject anything else, no open redirect), carried through the login form, and the fragment (#CODE) restored client-side since the server never sees it. Security-sensitive: review before shipping. Related: pf-ajt.4.

title: Join UX: room code, QR code, share link
description: Screen shows 4-letter code and a QR (small pure-JS QR encoder, no CDN). Phone joins via /room#CODE, remembers its name. Works inside /browse as a Room tab/sheet.
notes:
Built (uncommitted): roomclient/qr.js (from-scratch encoder, v1-10, L/M), room.joinUrl(), /room/qr.js route, /room-test shows code + QR + Copy link/Share and auto-joins on #CODE. Verified: qr-test.mjs decodes every length at both levels with jsQR (fails when format bits/BCH are broken on purpose); room-test.mjs decodes the page's QR from a screenshot and checks link auto-join. NOT yet scanned with a phone camera; deploy needed.
2026-10-10 phones: the QR as the Pixel renders it decodes to the join link (jsQR on a CDP screenshot). Opening the link on the Moto: by name it fails (Moto's Chrome cannot tunnel to pillowforrt.lan, ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED); by IP with a full navigation it auto-joins and goes direct. Fixes in tree (uncommitted): hello carries the box LAN IP and joinUrl() uses it; page listens for hashchange (a tab already on the page only gets a new fragment). Still unverified: a real camera scan; login drops #CODE (filed separately).
2026-10-10 second phone run (deployed 6658e3c): QR on the Pixel decodes; BUT room.lan came back 192.168.1.1 (the box has two LAN addresses: router .1 and services .254; 443 on .254 is DNAT'd to .1:3129, so the socket reports .1) and the phones are signed in at .254. Fixed in tree (uncommitted): roomLAN maps either to defaultDNSLocal[0]=.254, Go test. Verified on the phones with the .254 form of the link: DevTools navigation to it auto-joins and goes direct; a fragment-only change on a tab already on the page joins and drops the hash. An 'am start' VIEW intent opened a NEW tab on the Moto that stayed blank/loading (box answers instantly to curl; cause unknown, Moto had 9+ tabs). Camera scan still unverified.
2026-10-10 camera scan on the Moto: it opened Chrome on https://192.168.1.254/login#JCZE although the Moto was signed in. Cause: session cookie is SameSite=Strict, withheld from navigations that come from outside the site. Fix in tree (uncommitted): roomBounce (tiny same-site redirect page, ?b=1 marker) for /room-test; Go test + Chromium cross-site test with a no-bounce control. Needs deploy and a re-scan to confirm. The earlier blank-tab on 'am start' is probably the same family (external-app navigation) but unproven.
close_reason: Verified end to end on two phones: QR decodes, the Moto's camera scan opened Chrome, the bounce page carried the cookie through the SameSite=Strict navigation, the page auto-joined and the link went direct (84709f2, 5f5e5fa, 6658e3c).
